data.name: Zero Gravity
data.detailed_description:
This game is in its early stages and has been discontinued indefinitely and is now free. (May 2020)


Zero Gravity is a beautiful first-person/third-person puzzle-platformer simulation game where you will undergo four types of game modes. In Zero Gravity, you must really use your mind and patience in order to be able to progress through the game. (Zero Gravity is being recreated, find more info in the 'Early Access Description')

Puzzle Gamemode

In the Puzzle game mode, you will have to solve puzzling challenges that will require you to really use your mind and patience. You will have a suit that allows you to invert gravity so that you are able to walk on the ceiling and also have a jetpack boost that is useful for situations where you need to get up to somewhere.

EVA Gamemode

In the EVA game mode, you will be in full zero gravity environments where you will be required to solve space missions like repairing a satellite or rescue a ship that is falling back into Earth. You will have the abilities to use your suit thrusters to navigate around, however, you will have limited fuel which means you must use your fuel wisely.

Docking Gamemode

The Docking game mode is classed as a hardcore simulator which follows like-real science based from NASA. In this game mode, you will fly spaceships and attempt to dock with stations or other spaceships. This will require a lot of patience as the missions can take up to a long period depending on how familiar you are with the controls and science-based in space.

Platformer Gamemode

The Platformer game mode is a fun-casual mode where you will be placed in a zero gravity environment, but the player will have gravity. This means that some of the platforms you jump on in the levels may sink and some may even be explosive and cause you and the environment to go unstable. You will have a suit that is equipped with a zero gravity feature that has limited use and a jetpack that has rechargeable capabilities installed.

reviews.review: The project functions as a first-person and third-person puzzle-platformer simulation sandbox, attempting to reconstruct physics-driven environmental navigation within a fragmented early-access framework.Stylistically, the software introduces a versatile sub-genre taxonomy: the division of gameplay into four distinct modules—Puzzle, EVA space missions, NASA-inspired hardcore Docking simulation, and casual Platforming—offers immediate structural scale. The integration of zero-gravity thruster mechanics, fuel-management constraints, and gravity-inversion suite features successfully establishes a highly challenging operational matrix, generating a notable layer of surface-level engagement for physics enthusiasts during initial level trials.However, behind this multi-mode layout lies absolute developmental abandonment. The interactive core is permanently frozen inside an unstable 2016 beta matrix that was officially discontinued indefinitely and made free-to-play back in May 2020. The ambitious full-version promises—including a comprehensive RPG mechanic, outpost construction, and planet-to-planet space transit pipelines—remain completely absent from the architecture. This total cessation of support cuts the structural investigation short, rapidly collapsing a promising gravity simulation into an unpolished, abandoned technical showcase.Ultimately, this is a brief, unfinished digital artifact with minimal structural retention. While it offers friction-free utility as a free-to-play asset repository for curious operators investigating independent physics interfaces, anyone seeking a calibrated, fully realized interactive simulation with progressive mechanical feedback and closed-loop stability will face immediate, permanent stagnation.
